page.layout: Top: two medallion portraits side by side, each with its legend around the rim. Below them: one column of running text in two paragraphs. Below the text: a woodcut ornamental frame, no text. Running head at top; page number at top left.

main_text.p: FRANCISCUS Petrarca, natione Hetruscus, vir do-ctissimus, Philosophus, Rhetor, & Poëta celeberrimus, literas velut intermortuas quasi ab inferis revocauit:nec minus sancta conversatione quàm scientia claruit, multa opera tam in lingua Latina, quàm in sua vernacula conscripsit. Amore Christi & Philosophiæ salutaris vitam solitariam elegit, in qua Philoso-phando, orando & scribendo perseuerans, moritur in Eremi-torio suo agri Patauini, sub Carolo Imperatore huius nominis quarto, & Gregorio Papa huius nominis undecimo, anno à mundo condito 5536.à Christo nato 1374. Videto Trithemium.

IOANNES Boccatius Florentinus itidem Poëta, Philo-sophus, & Astronomus eruditissimus, multa præclara volumi-na tum Latino, tum vulgari suo idiomate conscripsit. moritur statim post Petrarcam. Videto etiam Trithemium.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed on the woodcut rim (left: FRANCISCVS PETRAR., right: IO. BOCCATI FLO. RHE.) and are transcribed above with v/u normalised. Long s read as plain s throughout. The woodcut ornament below the text carries no printed words. Page number read as 188; the first digit is slightly worn.
